segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
[... snow in Baghdad {OCR?}:
and it remained upon the surface of the earth for a week of days, about a cubit or a cubit and a half deep.
And likewise in all the land of Shinar:
namely in Basra and in Abadan,
and Mahruban,
and Jannaba,
a thing which had never again been heard of from of old.
And in this year there was a great abundance,
and a kor of wheat was sold for twelve dinars.
And there was a severe earthquake in the city of Dinawar,
and it destroyed many of the houses in it.
Sixteen thousand people were brought out from under the dust and buried,
besides those whom the earth opened up and swallowed.
And again a fierce black wind blew in Tikrit and in Daquqa,
and it destroyed many houses,
and uprooted a great number of palm trees and olive trees from their roots;
and large ships were sunk in the Sea of Persia.
And on the seventh of the month of Sha'ban of this year,
Abu Ali bar Zara'a, the Christian philosopher, died in Baghdad.
And in the same year, the people of a certain nation from the tribes of the inner Turks in the East, which is called Keraite,
believed in Christ,
and were discipled and baptized through a miracle that was performed with their king.
And at this time, al-Hakim, the caliph of Egypt, ordered (in Baghdad {OCR?}),
and the Church of the Resurrection in Jerusalem was demolished to the foundations,
and all its furnishings were plundered.
And he also destroyed thousands of churches that were in his realm.
And he ordered heralds to proclaim:
that every Christian {OCR: ܢܪܸܤܛܝܵܢܵܐ for ܟܪܸܤܛܝܵܢܵܐ} who enters the religion of the Arabs (Muslims)
shall be honored;
but he who does not enter shall be humiliated,
hanging a cross around his neck on the outside.
And the Jews shall hang around their necks the likeness of a calf's head,
that is to say, which they made in the wilderness and worshipped.
And they shall not wear rings on the right hand finger,
nor shall they ride horses,
except mules and donkeys with plain saddles and wooden stirrups.
And whoever does not accept this humilation,
let him take whatever he has
and go to the country of the Romans.
And when this decree went forth,
many went away,
and a few denied the Christian faith.
And those who neither emigrated nor apostatized,
hung crosses of gold and silver around their necks,
and made themselves saddles with superior, brightly colored cloths.
